\[

\[

\boxed{\displaystyle \frac{1}{12}}

assistant_message.content:
The pyramid is built by stacking the girls one on top of another, so the overall height is just the sum of the individual heights of the girls that actually form the pyramid.

**Which girls are in the pyramid?**  

- Bottom layer : 4 girls  
- Middle layer : 3 girls  
- Top layer : 2 girls  

That uses **4 + 3 + 2 = 9** girls.  
The problem tells us the **shortest girl is at the very top**, so we will take the 60‑inch girl for the top layer and the remaining eight girls to be the 64‑inch ones.

---

### 1. Sum the heights (in inches)

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Eight girls at 64 in each} &: 8 \times 64 = 512\ \text{in} \\
\text{One girl at 60 in}        &: 60\ \text{in} \\
\hline
\text{Total height}             &: 512 + 60 = 572\ \text{in}
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 2. Convert inches to feet  

\(1\text{ foot}=12\text{ inches}\), so

\[
\text{Height in feet} = \frac{572\ \text{in}}{12\ \text{in/ft}} = 47.666\ldots\ \text{ft}
\]

The fractional part corresponds to inches:

\[
0.666\ldots\ \text{ft} \times 12\ \frac{\text{in}}{\text{ft}} = 8\ \text{in}
\]

Hence  

\[
572\ \text{in} = 47\ \text{ft}\;8\ \text{in}
\]

---

\[
\boxed{47\ \text{feet}\;8\ \text{inches}}
\]
